provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-01-14T06 UTC: the Sun's centre is 1.08 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.06 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 91%, Earth in view 99%, both 90% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 332 Wh).
Longest darkness 21 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 368 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Marginal touchdown: the top of Earth's disc clears the skyline by under 0.5 deg; Earth is 0.06 deg above the skyline (bearing 162 deg, set by terrain 330 m away at 1.01 deg), so there is almost no margin for a landing error, a lower antenna or a later hour.
Darkest spell from 2029-01-26T19 UTC (21 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 190 deg, horizon -0.65 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2029-01-28T03 UTC (3 h): terrain 370 m away blocks it (bearing 151 deg: skyline 0.93 deg, centre of the body at -0.15 deg).
